stemMd: On which date did the Constitution of the Italian Republic enter into force?
explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** The question asks when the Constitution *entered into force*. That is the last step of a sequence - the Assembly that wrote it was elected, the text was approved, then promulgated, and only then did it take effect - and several of the dates offered belong to earlier or later steps.

**The fact that settles it.** The sequence runs:

- 2 June 1946: the institutional referendum chooses the Republic, and the Constituent Assembly is elected.
- 22 December 1947: the Constituent Assembly approves the text.
- 27 December 1947: the provisional head of state, Enrico De Nicola, promulgates it.
- 1 January 1948: the Constitution enters into force.

**How to check it.** The Constitution fixes its own start date: its final provision (the eighteenth of the Transitional and Final Provisions) states that it enters into force on 1 January 1948.

distractorRationale.a: 2 June 1946 is the date of the referendum that chose the Republic, now celebrated as Republic Day, and of the election of the Constituent Assembly. On that day the Constitution had not yet been written; the Assembly spent the next eighteen months drafting it.
distractorRationale.c: 22 December 1947 is when the Constituent Assembly approved the final text. Approval is not entry into force: the text was promulgated on 27 December 1947 and took effect on 1 January 1948.
distractorRationale.d: 18 April 1948 is the date of the first general election to the Parliament of the Republic. That election was held under the new Constitution, which was therefore already in force.
distractorRationale.e: 1 January 1958 is the date on which the Treaties of Rome, founding the European Economic Community and Euratom, entered into force - a different founding document, which took effect exactly ten years later.

accessibilityText: Question: on which date did the Constitution of the Italian Republic enter into force? The choices are 2 June 1946, 1 January 1948, 22 December 1947, 18 April 1948, and 1 January 1958.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank for the TIL-A History and general knowledge section (law and citizenship). Each distractor is a real date of the constitutional process or of a later founding treaty, so the item tests the difference between election, approval, entry into force and a later event.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The Constituent Assembly approved the Constitution on 22 December 1947, it was promulgated on 27 December 1947, and it entered into force on 1 January 1948. 2 June 1946 is the referendum, 18 April 1948 the first election, and 1 January 1958 the start of the EEC. C is the approval date, which is not the same as entry into force. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: The Constitution was approved on 22 December 1947, signed on 27 December and came into force on 1 January 1948. 2 June 1946 is the referendum, 18 April 1948 is the first election and 1958 is the EEC. The stem says 'enter into force', so C (the approval date) cannot be defended.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: Transitional and Final Provision XVIII sets entry into force on 1 January 1948. The other dates are the referendum and Constituent Assembly election (2 June 1946), approval (22 December 1947), the first republican general election (18 April 1948) and the entry into force of the Treaties of Rome (1 January 1958).
